name: The Seven-Day Streak
why_it_works: A tiny daily task with a visible streak taps the same pull as a game's login bonus: missing a day feels like losing progress. Commenting 'DAY 1' is a public promise, and people keep promises they make in front of others far more than private ones.

hook.pattern: Name a task so small it feels silly not to try, and attach a 7-day streak.
examples: This challenge is too easy to fail. That's the point.
Bet you can't keep this up seven days straight.

variables.name: daily_task
variables.description: The small daily action, 6 words or fewer, lowercase so it reads mid-sentence

variables.name: why_task
variables.description: One honest reason the task matters, 9 words or fewer, lowercase so it follows 'Because'
variables.example: it's the habit that makes every other habit easier

variables.name: streak_reward
variables.description: What finishers get on day 7, 6 words or fewer
variables.example: a free week of coached workouts

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a wall calendar with seven empty boxes circled in marker, morning light, a pair of sneakers or a product on the table in front, {{brand}} colors in the props
Vertical 9:16 candid lifestyle shot of a person doing {{daily_task}}, natural light, relaxed and real, not posed, face partly turned away

beats.voiceover: Every day, you check a box.

visual.prompt: Top-down vertical 9:16 hand marking check marks into seven calendar boxes one after another, quick stop-motion feel, warm morning light

beats.on_screen_text: Comment DAY 1 on {{start_day}}. Post your day number daily.
beats.voiceover: Comment DAY 1 on {{start_day}}. Then your day number, every day.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of the calendar with all seven boxes checked, a small gold star sticker on day seven, celebratory warm light

cta: Comment DAY 1 on {{start_day}} and follow {{brand}} for the daily check-in.

craft.notes: The task must be smaller than people expect, so the only reason to skip is laziness, not difficulty. Post a short daily check-in reel so the comment thread becomes the scoreboard and late joiners can still start.

do_not: Pick a task that needs equipment, money or an hour a day
Promise physical or skin results from seven days
Forget to deliver the day-7 reward; finishers will say so publicly
compliance: Supplements: no claims to diagnose, treat, cure or prevent disease; any structure/function claim needs the FDA disclaimer and real support
Skincare: cosmetic claims only (look, feel); no medical claims like 'heals' or 'cures acne', and no before/after photos without a 'results vary' disclaimer
Fitness challenges: tell people to check with a doctor before starting if they have health conditions; no weight-loss promises
Life coaches: no income, career or life-change promises; any result shown is labelled typical or not typical
